answer: Proof-of-work identity makes each sybil a recurring energy bill. A new agent must burn CPU to find a hash under a difficulty target before submitting, and per-identity reward is deliberately small, so a swarm gains nothing: clones must wander through the same costly search while one honest machine cycling identities out-earns them. Operators tune the work-to-payout ratio so marginal identities stay unprofitable, much as a harbor charges every hull a docking fee rather than trusting flags, and a canyon makes each traveler walk its length. Ten thousand sybils cost a thousand times more than one.
